subject: Creativity
title: Reframing: Same Problem, Different Lens
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Reframing: Same Problem, Different Lens.

hook.text: A hotel got complaints about slow elevators. Installing faster ones cost millions.

buildup.text: The problem wasn't slow elevators. It was boredom while waiting. Mirrors gave people something to do.

discovery.text: Reframing changes the problem definition — and the right definition is more than half the solution.

twist.text: Einstein supposedly said: 'If I had an hour to save the world, I'd spend 55 minutes defining the problem and 5 solving.

climax.text: Most creative breakthroughs aren't better answers. They're better questions.

punchline.text: Change the question. The answer changes itself.

quiz.question: How did the hotel solve the slow elevator complaint?
options: Added mirrors to reduce perceived wait time

details.summary: Reframing changes the way a problem is defined rather than how it is solved. By shifting the question, entirely new solution spaces open up. Einstein said that if he had one hour to save the world, he would spend 55 minutes defining the problem.
details.whyItMatters: Most failed creative efforts fail because they solved the wrong problem. Reframing is the most powerful and underused creative skill because it transforms the entire solution landscape.
takeaways: Reframing changes the problem definition rather than the solution
A well-framed problem is often half-solved already
Multiple frames of the same problem reveal different opportunities

faq.question: How do you reframe a problem?
faq.answer: Ask the question differently. Instead of how do we sell more, ask why are customers leaving. Instead of how do we make this faster, ask what would happen if speed did not matter. Each reframe opens a different solution space.

faq.question: Is reframing the same as lateral thinking?
faq.answer: They overlap but are distinct. Lateral thinking is a broad approach to non-linear problem solving. Reframing specifically targets the problem definition itself. Reframing is one technique within the broader lateral thinking toolkit.
